novel_features.name: Campaign cap headroom
novel_features.description: See which launched campaigns are sending below their daily cap, at cap, or idle, in one table.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining each campaign's daily-cap setting against per-day sent-email counts that only exist together in the local store; no single API call returns 'below cap'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs to find under-delivering campaigns across an account without opening every campaign in the UI.

novel_features.name: Sender health board
novel_features.description: One board joining sender state, attached campaigns, and recent bounces to spot dead or over-assigned inboxes.
novel_features.rationale: Sender state, campaign attachment, and bounce signal are separate API surfaces; only a local join shows 'disconnected AND still on 3 live campaigns'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before a deliverability audit to find senders that are degraded but still actively sending.

novel_features.name: Interested-reply roll-up
novel_features.description: Every reply marked interested across all campaigns since a timestamp, joined to its lead, campaign, and sender.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates interested replies across campaigns into one time-windowed view the per-campaign endpoints cannot return in a single call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for a daily 'what got interested since yesterday' triage across the whole account.

novel_features.name: Stale-lead detector
novel_features.description: Find leads stuck mid-sequence: in a live campaign, already emailed, no reply, and no scheduled next send.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining leads, scheduled_emails, sent_emails, and replies with date math that no single endpoint exposes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use weekly to surface leads silently rotting in a sequence so they can be re-engaged or cleaned out.

novel_features.name: Sequence-variant win rates
novel_features.description: Per A/B sequence-step variant, the reply rate and interested rate computed from local data.
novel_features.rationale: Joins sequence_steps variants against sent_emails and replies in SQLite to produce per-variant rates no endpoint returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when deciding which subject/body variant to keep in a multi-step campaign.

novel_features.name: Launch readiness preflight
novel_features.description: Before resuming, check locally that a campaign has a schedule, at least one step, a sender, leads, and that every merge tag exists as a custom variable.
novel_features.rationale: Validates the full launch chain by joining campaign, schedule, sequence, sender, and custom-variable state and set-checking merge tags against custom variables.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this before launch to catch broken {VARIABLE} renders and missing senders that would silently kill a send.

novel_features.name: Reply triage queue
novel_features.description: An oldest-first worklist of pending replies with lead and campaign context, ready to pipe into mark-interested or follow-up push.
novel_features.rationale: Filters and sorts the local reply store with joined context into an agent-shaped queue that drives the existing action commands.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use as the entry point for a morning master-inbox triage loop an agent can work top to bottom.

narrative.headline: Every Email Bison campaign, lead, and reply on the command line, plus a local database and cross-entity analytics no other Email Bison tool has.
narrative.value_prop: A Go CLI for the Email Bison cold-email API with a local SQLite store, cursor-based sync, and offline FTS. Beyond mirroring every endpoint, it answers questions a single API call cannot: which campaigns are under their daily cap (campaigns headroom), which senders are degraded but still live (sender-emails health), which leads are stuck mid-sequence (leads stale), and which A/B variant is winning (campaigns variants).
narrative.auth_narrative: Email Bison is self-hosted: each workspace has its own dedicated instance domain. Set EMAIL_BISON_BASE_URL to your instance (default https://dedi.emailbison.com) and EMAIL_BISON_API_KEY to a workspace api-user token from Settings -> Developer API. Every token is scoped to one workspace.

quickstart.comment: confirm the base URL and token resolve and the API is reachable
pull campaigns, leads, senders, and replies into the local store
see which campaigns are sending below their daily cap
roll up interested replies from the last day

troubleshoots.fix: Set EMAIL_BISON_API_KEY to a valid api-user token and confirm EMAIL_BISON_BASE_URL points at your dedicated instance, not dedi.emailbison.com.
Each api-user token is scoped to one workspace; use the token minted inside the target workspace.
The API allows about 10 requests/second; the client backs off on the retry_after header, so let the sync finish rather than re-running it.

troubleshoots.symptom: Merge tags render empty in a campaign
troubleshoots.fix: Run campaigns preflight <id>; every {VARIABLE} in a sequence body must exist as a custom variable in the workspace.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or operator needs to run or audit Email Bison outreach programmatically: launching and pausing campaigns, ingesting and tagging leads, triaging the master inbox, and answering cross-entity questions (cap headroom, sender health, stale leads, variant win rates) that the web UI and raw API cannot answer in one shot. It shines for agencies running many workspaces who want scriptable, offline-queryable campaign state.
